breadcrumb: Std 9 Social Science (English) — History Unit 5: The Classical World — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Classical World comprises ancient Greece and Rome. Classical Age refers to the inter-locking civilisation of ancient Greece and ancient Rome, known as Graeco-Roman World.

en.q: The inter-locking civilisation of ancient Greece and Rome is known as the:

ta.q: பண்டைய கிரேக்கமும் ரோமும் இணைந்த நாகரிகம் எவ்வாறு அழைக்கப்படுகிறது?

questions.quote: Acropolis, a fortified city of ancient Greeks on a hill in Athens. The Olympic festival of sports and games bound the city-states together. Age of Tyrants 6th–4th century BCE.

en.q: The Greek city-states were bound together by trade, a common alphabet, similar religious practices and:
options: festivals such as the Olympic games
en.explanation: The Olympic festival is the illustrious example.

ta.q: கிரேக்க நகர அரசுகள் வணிகம், பொது எழுத்து, சமய வழக்கங்கள் ஆகியவற்றுடன் எதன் மூலம் இணைந்திருந்தன?
ta.explanation: ஒலிம்பிக் விளையாட்டு விழா இதற்குச் சிறந்த எடுத்துக்காட்டு.

questions.quote: Athenian democracy: law-making power vested in an assembly open to all freemen; judges and lower officials chosen by lots. 'Democracy' excluded slaves, women and non-residents known as metics (traders and craftsmen). Democracy survived in Athens for about 200 years.

en.q: Which of the following was excluded from the Athenian 'democracy'?
options: Citizens chosen by lot as judges
en.explanation: Slaves, women and metics were excluded.

questions.quote: Pericles (461–429 BCE) held power for thirty years. Athens and Sparta were continuously at war (Peloponnesian War). Historians call this the Age of Pericles. Socrates was accused of refusing to accept the gods recognized by the State and corrupting the youth; sentenced to die by drinking hemlock.

en.q: Socrates was sentenced to death by drinking:
en.explanation: Hemlock, a poison, after being accused of corrupting the youth.

ta.q: சாக்ரடீஸுக்கு மரண தண்டனையாக எதைக் குடிக்கக் கொடுக்கப்பட்டது?
ta.explanation: இளைஞர்களைக் கெடுத்ததாகக் குற்றம்சாட்டப்பட்டு நஞ்சு அருந்தும் தண்டனை பெற்றார்.

questions.quote: Marius became Consul with the support of the equites (new rich class). Civil war between the followers of Marius and Sulla. Sulla reigned for three years as a virtual dictator.

options: the new rich or propertied class below the Senatorial class
en.explanation: Equites were the new rich below the rank of the Senatorial class.

options: செனட்டர் தகுதிக்குக் கீழ் உள்ள புதுப் பணக்காரர், சொத்துடையோர்
ta.explanation: ஈக்விட்டுகள் செனட்டர் வகுப்புக்குக் கீழ் உள்ள புதிய செல்வந்த வகுப்பு.

questions.quote: The revolt of Spartacus began in 73 BCE involving about 70,000 slaves. Ultimately Spartacus was killed and 6,000 of his followers were executed.

en.q: The famous Roman slave revolt led by Spartacus began in:
en.explanation: It involved about 70,000 slaves; 6,000 followers were executed.

ta.q: ஸ்பார்டகஸ் தலைமையிலான புகழ்பெற்ற ரோமானிய அடிமை எழுச்சி எப்போது தொடங்கியது?

questions.quote: Han dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), founded by Liu Pang, flourished for 400 years. Capital Chang-an. Wu Ti drove away the Huns. The Silk Road linked China with the West. Silk went westward; wools, gold and silver went east. China received Buddhism from India via the Silk Road.

en.q: The capital of the Han dynasty was:

questions.quote: Jesus was tried and crucified. After his crucifixion, St Paul started spreading the Christian doctrine. Christians' refusal to pay respect to the Emperor's image was viewed as political treason. Constantine became a Christian; Christianity became the official religion of the Empire.

en.q: Why were Christians persecuted by Rome?
options: They refused to pay taxes to Greece
They opposed the Roman senate's laws on trade
Their refusal to honour the Emperor's image was seen as political treason
en.explanation: Refusal to pay respect to the Emperor's image was viewed as treason.

options: பேரரசரின் உருவத்தை வணங்க மறுத்தது அரசியல் துரோகமாகக் கருதப்பட்டது
ta.explanation: பேரரசரின் உருவத்தை மதிக்க மறுத்தது அரசியல் துரோகமாகக் கருதப்பட்டது.

questions.quote: The Kushan Empire is said to have sent an embassy to Augustus Caesar. Sangam literature hailed as first secular literature of India. Teakwood, pepper, pearls, ivory exported from the Malabar Coast to Babylonia, Egypt, Greece and Rome.

en.q: According to the book, Sangam literature is hailed as the first ____ literature of India.
en.explanation: Sangam literature is hailed as the first secular literature of India.

ta.q: நூலின்படி சங்க இலக்கியம் இந்தியாவின் முதல் ____ இலக்கியம் எனப் போற்றப்படுகிறது.
ta.explanation: சங்க இலக்கியம் இந்தியாவின் முதல் சமயச்சார்பற்ற இலக்கியம்.
